 SIR G M ANANDA, ADVOCATE FOR R3)
 THIS W.P. IS FILED PRAYING TO-DIRECT THE RESPONDENTS TO ACQUIRE THE PORTION OF THE LAND IN THE LAND BEARING MUNICIPAL KATHA NO.D7/2309/2288-10840/4873 SITUATED AT MANDYA- MALAVALLI ROAD, MANDYA CITY AS SHOWN IN THE SKETCH PREPARED BY CIVIL ENGINEER VIDE ANNX-J AND PAY THE COMPENSATION AS PER THE PROVISIONS OF THE RIGHT TO FAIR COMPENSATION AND TRANSPARENCY IN LAND ACQUISITION, REHABILATION AND RESETTLEMENT ACT, 2013 AND ETC.
 THIS PETITION, COMING ON FOR FURTHER HEARING, THIS DAY, THE COURT MADE THE FOLLOWING:
 ORDER 1.

The petitioners are before this Court seeking for the following relief's:
(i) Issue writ in the nature of mandamus directing the respondents to acquire the portion of the land in the land bearing Municipal Katha No.D7/2309/2288:10840/
4873 situated at Mandya-Malavalli Road, Mandya City as shown in the sketch prepared by civil Engineer marked as Annexure "J" and pay the compensation as per the NC: 2023:KHC:39539 provisions of the Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, 2013;
(ii) Issue writ in the nature of mandamus directing the respondents to pay the compensation towards depriving the petitioners from developing their land bearing Municipal Katha No.D7/2309/ 2288:10840/4873 situated at Mandya- Malavalli Road, Mandya City by taking into consideration the cost of construction prevailing in the year 2002 and the construction prevailing as on today and such other factors in the interest of justice;
S B Boregowda vs State Of Karnataka on 6 November, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/155097361/
2 (iii) Declare that the resolutions dated 30.03.2002 bearing No.3/2002 passed on subject No.8 marked as Annexure "B" and the resolution dated 25.05.2004 bearing No.2/2004-2005 passed on subject No.69(5) are illegal and unenforceable in law.
2.

sentences.text: The petitioners are the owners of the land bearing katha No.D7/2309/2288:10840/4873 measuring 1333 square meters situated at Mandya-Malavalli Main Road, Mandya City and the said property comes within the jurisdiction of Mandya City Municipal Council (MCMC).

The MCMC having collected the layout plan charges had issued katha in respect of the said property in favour of the father of the NC: 2023:KHC:39539 petitioners which came to be inherited by the petitioners by way of succession.

In the comprehensive development plan which has come into force, the portion of the land of the petitioners was earmarked for formation of a deviation road i.e., Guttalu to Gubehalla from the Mandya-Malavalli main road measuring approximately 30x165 feet.
3. In pursuance thereto, a resolution had been passed by MCMC on 30.03.2002 resolving to acquire the said land in terms of the designation made in the CDP.

However, the same has not been followed thereafter and subsequently, the MCMC made an offer to the petitioners to purchase the land at Sub-Registrar value of Rs.10,48,600/- which the petitioners accepted in the fond of receiving the money at the earliest.
However, the said payments were not made in 2004 but were paid in installments from 15.02.2008 to 14.05.2010 to an extent of Rs.7,50,000/-.
Thus, even as on 14.05.2010, the NC: 2023:KHC:39539 entire amounts had not been paid.

Hence, the petitioners had written a letter to MCMC to make payment of the balance amount and register the property since till then, there is no sale deed has been executed by the petitioners in favour of MCMC.
4. Despite the notice which had been issued, no action has been taken by MCMC and MCMC continued to be quiet.

Hence, the petitioners issued one more notice on 21.07.2014 informing the MCMC that the petitioners does not wish to proceed with the transaction and if at all, the MCMC wanted to make use of the land of the petitioners, they could do so by way of acquisition under the Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, 2013 and thereafter, there appears to be several correspondences which have been exchanged between the MCMC, the Director, Municipal Administration and the District Collector in the year NC: 2023:KHC:39539 2017 and finally, a letter came to be issued on 17.11.2017 calling upon the petitioners to register the land by receiving the balance amount.

entities.text: Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, 2013
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text:
This letter was issued on 17.11.2017 that means after the lapse of more than three years from the notice dated 21.07.2014 issued by the petitioners.
5. On 21.02.2019, a letter was issued by the Municipal Commissioner calling upon the petitioners for negotiation to resolve the issue.

The petitioners have informed the Commissioner that they are not ready to go on with the transaction and they called upon them either to acquire the land or return the amount but neither was done, hence, the petitioners have filed above petition seeking for the above reliefs.
6. The learned counsel Sri Mahesh R Uppin appearing for the petitioners would submit that from the year 2004 till now, the petitioners have been made to run from pillar to post.

The respondents have promised NC: 2023:KHC:39539 to make payment of the market value of the property on S B Boregowda vs State Of Karnataka on 6 November, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/155097361/
3 25.05.2004 but till date that amount has not been paid and when the petitioners extended and accepted the installments paid by MCMC from 2008 to 2010, even then, the full amount was not paid and in that background left with no option

sentences.text: , the petitioners have called upon the MCMC to acquire the land vide legal notice dated 21.07.2014.
The petitioners are not willing to go ahead with the said agreement and refuted the said agreement.
The respondents have not taken any action thereon.
Hence, the petitioners are constrained to approach this Court.

The property by the petitioners demarcated in the CDP for the purpose of road and the same could only be acquired in terms of Section 69 of the Karnataka Town and Country Planning Act, 1961 (for short 'the Act of 1961') and as such, if at all, the respondents make use of the land of the petitioners, it is only the provisions under Section 69 of the Act of 1961 which can be made use of by the respondents.

entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text: On the NC: 2023:KHC:39539 above grounds, he submits that the above petition required to be allowed.

7. The learned counsel Sri Ananda appearing for respondent No.3 would submit that way-back in the year 2010 itself nearly 80% of the amount has been paid inasmuch as Rs.7,50,000/- had been paid to the petitioners and subsequent thereto, the respondents were willing to make payment of the balance amount which has conveyed vide its letter dated 01.07.2014 and the petitioners have not accepted the said request, the dispute has arisen.
Though MCMC is willing to make payment of the amount, the relief which has been sought by the petitioners cannot be granted.

8. Heard the learned counsel appearing for the petitioners and the learned counsel appearing for the respondents and perused the material available on record.
NC: 2023:KHC:39539 9.

The present case is a classic case of abuse of power resorted to by MCMC - respondent No.3 knowing fully well that in terms of Section 69 of the Act of 1961, the land of the petitioners was required to be acquired under the relevant land acquisition Act prevalent at that point of time, even though resolution has been passed, prevailing upon the petitioners to accept the guideline value,
which the petitioners accepted in the fond of receiving the money at the earliest as could be seen from the letter of the petitioners which has been addressed to the MCMC dated 14.08.2004.

This hope of the petitioners was completely dashed and the respondents continued to exercise their dominant position in the matter by not making payment of the amounts till the year 2008 when the MCMC started making payment of installments to a tune of Rs.50,000/- each commencing from 07.02.2008 which was also not paid monthly but whenever the respondents felt like making payment, the same has - 10 - NC: 2023:KHC:39539 been done in a erratic manner without any sequencing of the payment, till 04.05.2010, an amount of Rs.7,50,000/- was paid and thereafter there was complete silence on the part of MCMC till the year 2014 when an offer was made to make payment of balance amount which came to be refuted by the petitioners by issuing legal notice dated 21.07.2014.

S B Boregowda vs State Of Karnataka on 6 November, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/155097361/
4 10.

sentences.text: Thereafter, there was complete silence on the part of MCMC until 17.11.2017 when a demand was made to register the sale deed by accepting the balance amount.
Thereafter on 21.02.2019, an offer was made by the Municipal Commissioner for re- negotiation to settle the matter amicably.

The above dates would only indicate the manner in which MCMC by using its dominant position prevailed upon hapless land owner in trying to takeover their land inasmuch as without making the payment of due amount.

Even now, when the matter was taken up by this Court, the learned counsel appearing for the petitioners submits that suitable enhancement could be made to the amount agreed, even then,
MCMC has not agreed to pay any reasonable amount acceptable to the petitioners except to state that MCMC is ready to make payment of remaining amount of Rs.1,41,000/- with the bank rate of interest.
12. I find the said stand of MCMC is completely unacceptable, unreasonable, arbitrary and a fraud on power by sticking to abuse its dominant position.

The Municipal Authority does not have right to acquire the property from the land owners without following the due procedure, prevail upon the land owners to agree to sell the property by promising payment of the consideration amount at the earliest and thereafter act in a lackadaisical manner without making such payment for nearly 17 years.
In that - 12 - NC: 2023:KHC:39539 view of the matter, the action on the part of MCMC is liable to be deprecated.

13. In the above circumstances, I pass the following:
ORDER (i) The respondents are at liberty to acquire the land of the petitioners under the provisions of the Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition,
Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, 2013 if they so desire, by prevailing upon the Government to issue a notification within a period of 90 days from today.

entities.text:
Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition,
Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, 2013
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text: (ii) In the event of no such notification being issued, MCMC shall connect the plan which has been submitted by the petitioners for the development of entire land including the area demarcated for the road.

The Planning Authority shall consider the plan if any submitted by the petitioners for - 13 - S B Boregowda vs State Of Karnataka on 6 November, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/155097361/
5 NC: 2023:KHC:39539 development of their land without reference to the claim of MCMC on the said land in accordance with the applicable rules relating thereto.

(iii) Needless to say that if no acquisition notification is issued, the petitioners having submitted a plan for approval then, the amount of Rs.7,50,000/- received by the petitioners shall be returned to MCMC with interest at the rate of 6% per annum prior to making such application for sanction of plan.
(iv) In the event of acquisition notification being issued, the amount of Rs.7,50,000/- shall be adjusted towards compensation liable to be paid to the petitioners.
(v) If no acquisition notification is issued then the petitioners filing an application for the entire land for issuance of katha/e-katha of the property and MCMC shall consider the - 14 - NC: 2023:KHC:39539 same and act on the same and issue e- katha within a period of thirty days from such application being made.

Sd/-
